correctness.rationale: For all integers q>=2, a>=r>=1, the single-ball recoloring coupling proves balanced finite populations maximize hypergeometric completion, including strictness using a degenerate random population. Explicit differentiation of paired iid binomial-tail completion establishes unique strict uniform maximum. Dirichlet mixture implies the strict reinforced inequality. Beta-binomial fixed-deficit asymptotics and a uniform O(k^-2a) pair-overlap bound give the precise power-law coefficient and moment cutoff. The exact-rational checker passed 79 triples, 237 independent comparisons and 45 tail checks; this is supplementary finite evidence, not a universal proof.

originality.rationale: No exact claim equivalent to the combined strict balanced three-mode all-horizon q-color r-copy completion ordering AND the explicit simultaneous Pólya tail coefficient/moment cutoff was found in actual published-finding corpus searches, the inspected primary paper or relevant classic work. Jacobs defines the associated three negative urn laws and does not settle this multicolor comparison; Anceaume et al. optimize iid coupons under a different premise; Henze and Holmes give individual-color Pólya waiting-time results. Classical majorization, exchangeability and beta-binomial components are not claimed novel in isolation. The risk of unindexed historical implication remains.
residual_risks: A differently worded classical majorization or urn occupancy theorem could imply all or part of the finite-time stochastic inequalities; online search and inspected primary papers do not prove absolute novelty.
A general Dirichlet-multinomial coupon-collector asymptotic in an unindexed source might cover the q-color r-copy constant.
The generalized reinforced stochastic approximation reference was abstract-only; this does not demonstrate full-document noncoverage.

value.rationale: The common balanced urn creates a mathematically natural comparison of sampling without replacement, iid replacement and classical reinforcement under the same all-color target. The theorem supplies a complete strict stochastic hierarchy for all feasible q,a,r at every horizon and an exact reinforced tail coefficient plus a sharp fractional-moment boundary, distinguishing bounded, exponential and polynomial-tail completion in a way relevant to reliability, occupancy and coverage-time analysis. It is not an unmotivated numerical slice or textbook parameter substitution.
